title: yq for YAML
intro: Work from the module directory. Use Mike Farah **`yq`** v4+ for questions 1–9; question 10 uses text tools only.

questions.prompt: **`manifest.yaml`** is a Kubernetes Deployment manifest. What is the value of `metadata.name`?
From **`manifest.yaml`**, print every `spec.containers[].image`, one per line, in document order.
**`settings.yaml`** holds application configuration. What is the value of `database.host`?
**`jobs.yaml`** defines a list of scheduled jobs. List all job IDs in alphabetical order, one per line.
From **`jobs.yaml`**, how many jobs have a `priority` strictly greater than `5`?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
yq '[.jobs[] | select(.priority > 5)] | length' jobs.yaml
```

`select(.priority > 5)` filters to matching jobs; wrapping in `[…]` collects them into an array so `length` can count them.

questions.prompt: **`inventory.yaml`** has an `items` list where each item has a `qty` field. What is the total quantity across all items?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
yq '[.items[].qty] | add' inventory.yaml
```

Or using shell arithmetic:
```bash
yq -r '.items[].qty' inventory.yaml | awk '{s+=$1} END{print s}'
```

`[.items[].qty]` collects all qty values into an array; `add` sums them. The `awk` alternative works when the values are integers.

questions.prompt: **`stacked.yaml`** contains two YAML documents separated by `---`. What is the `kind` of each document? List them in order, one per line.
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
yq -r '.kind' stacked.yaml
```

`yq` iterates all documents in the file when you use `.kind` without a document index filter.

questions.prompt: Convert **`manifest.yaml`** to JSON and print it as a single compact line with no indentation.
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
yq -o=json -I=0 '.' manifest.yaml
```

`-o=json` selects JSON output; `-I=0` sets indentation to 0 (compact).

questions.prompt: **`profile.yaml`** uses YAML merge anchors to share base configuration between environments. After merge resolution, what is the value of `production.timeout_ms`?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
yq -r '.production.timeout_ms' profile.yaml
```

yq v4 (Mike Farah) resolves YAML merge anchors (`<<:`) automatically. The `production` mapping explicitly sets `timeout_ms: 2000`, which overrides the inherited base value, so the result is `2000`.

questions.prompt: **`manifest.canon.txt`** is a plain-text copy of the manifest (no `yq` available). Using only text-processing tools, extract the value of the `tier` label.
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
grep 'tier:' manifest.canon.txt | awk '{print $2}'
```

Or simply `grep -oP 'tier: \K\S+'` if GNU grep is available.

summaryMarkdown:
## Learning outcomes

- Read nested keys and **walk arrays** with Mike Farah **`yq`** expressions.
- Choose **raw output** (`-r`) vs structured output for downstream tools.
- Handle **multi-document** YAML with `yq` document iteration.
- Convert YAML to **compact JSON** for piping into **`jq`**, HTTP clients, or checksums.
- Understand **merge anchors** (`<<:`) and how overrides interact with inherited values.
- Recognize **`yq` is not universal**: the **Mike Farah** and **kislyuk** tools share a name but differ in flags and semantics.

## Scope

**In scope:** query, filter, emit JSON, multi-doc reads, one text-only drill (`grep`/`awk`/`sed`) on a canonical-style excerpt. **Out of scope:** full **Kubernetes** schema validation, **JSONPath** servers, in-place **`yq -i`** editing workflows.
